nodes.label: Vision
nodes.sublabel: where we want to get to
nodes.description:
A picture of how life gets better for the people you help. The "after" picture.

• Write about their life, not your product.
• One or two sentences.
• No money, no numbers.

Real example (Delivery CRM):
Owners spend their days growing their business, not holding it together.

nodes.label: Target audience
nodes.description:
The exact group of people you build this for. Start small, with a group you could list name by name.

One sentence:
[Role] of a [type of business] in [place], with [size], who [trigger] and needs to [job].

Check yourself:
• Can you name real people in the group?
• Do you know where to find them?
• Have you talked to at least one of them?

Real example (Delivery CRM):
An owner of a carpet and furniture cleaning business in Lviv, with 3 to 4 people including the owner, who is frustrated by searching for order and customer data in notebooks, Excel and chats, and who misses orders, and needs to structure the business data.

nodes.label: Desired outcomes
nodes.description:
The concrete results your audience wants, on the way to the vision. Think of the drill:

• Nobody wants a drill. That is the product.
• They want a hole. That is an outcome: concrete, and they would notice it.
• They want the hole to hang a picture. That is the bigger result, close to the vision.

Write each outcome as one line: less (or more) of something, in a moment they know. Keep 3 to 5.

Delivery CRM:
• Drill: a CRM app.
• Hole: less time finding an order, fewer missed orders.
• Picture on the wall: owners spend their days growing their business.

nodes.label: Choose desire to validate
nodes.description:
One claim about the present that you test next. It is a decision, not research.

• Format: we validate that [audience] [feel / do this] when [situation].
• One feeling or one behavior per statement.
• No product words and no numbers.
• It comes from one desired outcome.

Delivery CRM: owners feel overwhelmed when they search for an order.
Online shop: visitors leave the cart when they see the shipping cost.

nodes.label: Hypotheses + bar
nodes.description:
Turn the claim into hypotheses, each with a success bar set before testing.

• One hypothesis per aspect: frequency, cost, workaround, feeling.
• Each has a number: how many people, and how many of them.
• Write the bar before the first call and do not move it.
• Add the verdict rule: what counts as validated.

nodes.label: Choose how to validate
nodes.description:
Choose a method for each hypothesis, and what you need to start.

• Match the method to the bar: interview, show me, observation, survey, community or review mining, or existing data.
• Prefer what people do over what they say.
• Choose the cheapest honest method.
• Methods with no people can start today.

Online shop: the order and checkout data you already have.

nodes.label: Validate
nodes.description:
Run the methods. Start with the validation profile, then talk to the people or read the data.

• Profile: who, how many, which methods, what counts.
• Ask about the last real case, never "would you".
• Write each piece of evidence into the evidence log as it comes.

nodes.label: Evidence log
nodes.description:
One row per piece of evidence, written while you validate.

• The exact words or the number, not your summary.
• Which hypothesis it supports.
• For or against.
• Unprompted or asked.
• Who it came from, so you can check the audience later.

nodes.label: Result + decision
nodes.description:
Count, compare with the bar, apply the verdict rule, then decide.

• Count the people for and against each hypothesis.
• Compare each count with its bar.
• Verdict: validated, not validated or unclear.
• Decision: keep, narrow, change or stop.
• Read the strongest evidence against first.

nodes.label: Share
nodes.description:
Share what you learned in public. It builds your personal brand.

• An X post: the finding and the number.
• A portfolio case: the claim, the method, the result.
• Share the real result, including a failed one.
• Leave out anything that identifies a person or a business.

nodes.label: Gate
nodes.description:
The last check before layer 2.

• The bars were not moved.
• The sample was reached.
• The audience was right.
• The verdict rule is met.
• The evidence against was read.
• The decision is keep.

Result: pass writes the validated opportunity. Not yet means more evidence. Fail means a new lap.

nodes.label: Validated opportunity
nodes.description:
A proven fact that stands between you and the desired outcome. Written only when the gate passes. It is the one thing that crosses from layer 1 into layer 2.

It can be:
• the audience's pain,
• a behavior you see in your data,
• a problem of your own business.

It holds the fact, its strongest evidence, the strongest evidence against, and what is still unknown.

Delivery CRM: owners feel overwhelmed when they search for an order. Evidence: owners described a last case.
Online shop: visitors leave the cart at the shipping cost. Evidence: the checkout data of the last 90 days.
Any subscription: new subscribers cancel in the first two months.

nodes.label: Explore solutions
nodes.sublabel: how might we solve this problem?
nodes.description:
Turn the validated opportunity into one question, then list ways to answer it.

• Question: how might we solve this problem? Name who it is for: the audience or your own business.
• List 3 to 5 possible solutions.
• Draw on their processes, interview stories, social media and community research, and competitors.

Delivery CRM: how might we help owners find an order without searching notebooks?
Online shop: how might we reduce cart abandonment at the shipping cost, to raise the average cart?

nodes.label: Pick one solution
nodes.description:
Choose one solution from the list.

• The one with the strongest evidence.
• The one you can test cheaply.
• One change per lap, so you know what worked.
• Write one line on why you left the others out.

nodes.label: Hypotheses + bar
nodes.description:
If we do this, the outcome improves from X to Y. Written before building.

• Name the solution and the metric, with the baseline and the target.
• Add what must not get worse, for example conversion.
• Add the sample size and how long the test runs.
• Do not move the bar after you see data.

Online shop: free shipping above a cart value raises the average cart from X to Y, and conversion falls by no more than Z.

nodes.label: Choose how to validate
nodes.description:
Choose how to test the solution. Same rules as in layer 1, with stronger methods.

• Prefer what people do or pay over what they say.
• Write down what you need first: traffic, access, tools.

Online shop: an A/B test, where half of the visitors see the change.
Delivery CRM: a smoke test page, a paid pilot or a pre-sale.

nodes.label: Minimal requirements
nodes.description:
The smallest version that can answer the hypothesis.

• List only what the test needs.
• Cut everything else for this lap.
• Define done: what you can observe when it works.

Online shop: one banner or one cart rule, not a new checkout.

nodes.label: Build
nodes.description:
Build the smallest version, fast, with AI.

• Build only the requirements.
• Use AI for code, copy and layout.
• Stop when the test can run, not when it looks finished.
• Keep a way to switch it off.

nodes.label: Validate
nodes.description:
Run the test with real users and real data.

• Start the test and write down the date.
• Do not change the solution or the bar while it runs.
• Wait for the planned sample, not for a good-looking result.
• Write each result into the evidence log.

nodes.label: Evidence log
nodes.description:
One row per result of the test, the same as in layer 1.

• The number per variant: orders, sign-ups or payments.
• Which hypothesis it supports.
• For or against.
• The sample so far.
• Anything unexpected you saw, even if it is not in the hypothesis.

nodes.label: Result + decision
nodes.description:
Count, compare with the bar, decide, and let the evidence change the next steps.

• Compare the result with the bar from the hypothesis.
• Decision: keep, narrow, change or stop.
• If the evidence shows the opportunity itself was wrong, go back to layer 1.

nodes.label: Share
nodes.description:
Share the result in public. It builds your personal brand.

• An X post: the change, the number, what you learned.
• A portfolio case: the opportunity, the solution, the result.
• Share the real result, including a failed one.
• Leave out anything that identifies a person or a business.

nodes.label: Next lap or layer
nodes.description:
Decide what happens next from the evidence.

• Keep: go to the next layer, for example roll out to everyone or test a bigger change.
• Narrow or change: next lap from Pick one solution, with a smaller segment or another solution.
• Stop: back to Explore solutions.
• Wrong opportunity: back to layer 1.
